turns.summary: Rhinofire wakes in the Marchward on an early-spring morning: water-crisis talk at every table, border-watchfulness thick in the air, and Marrow noting the treeline.
turns.narration:
Morning in the Marchward comes in gray and cold, early-spring damp pressing through every gap in the timber-and-stone buildings that line the main track. The mud is real mud — boot-deep at the crossing, crusted at the edges where last night's freeze didn't quite finish. You stand outside the hostel where you slept, Marrow perched on the eave above your head with its wings slightly open, drying them against the pale sky. The bird looks down at you once, then back at the treeline to the west, where the Redline's edge begins.

The Marchward is awake and moving. At the long trestle outside the common-house, a Redline duelist in worn leathers — the horizontal scar across her collarbone the formal mark of a witnessed bout — shares a bench with a Stillhold exile whose grey robe has been patched three times over. They are not speaking but they are sharing the same pot of barley, which here counts as peace. The talk at the other tables is low and watchful: border-talk, the kind that moves in short sentences and pauses before proper nouns. You catch fragments — 'upstream,' 'the sickness is real this time,' 'Harmonic said the Radiant, the Radiant said the Harmonic, and meanwhile my cousin's children—'

The water crisis has found even this far-edge town. The Marchward runs on a spring-fed cistern separate from the valley's main flow, but travelers come through with news on their boots and bad news travels fastest. There is a barrel of boiled water outside the common-house with a wooden ladle and a sign scratched into the stave: DO NOT DRINK UNTREATED. Your waterskin, filled at the last clean spring, feels suddenly more valuable. Something else moves under the talk — a word you've now heard twice since you stepped outside, from two different clusters of people: 'the substrate.' A mason's apprentice said it to her journeyman. A Marcher trader said it to no one in particular, then looked at his hand as if he'd felt something in it. What Wakes Beneath is not valley gossip anymore. It has arrived here.

Marrow drops from the eave and lands on your pack-strap, settles its weight, and says nothing. Which is its comment.

personalArc.name: The Weight of the Net
personalArc.premise: A fisher from the edge of the world who put down the blade — or was put down by it — carries the Marchward in their hands and a village in their chest, and must decide whether righting wrongs means picking the blade back up, or finding something the blade was never built to fix.
personalArc.stakes: To hold the line they chose when they walked away, or discover that walking away was itself the wound they have been circling — and that the village they came from is the thing the world will eventually ask them to pay with.
